insights.title: Preserve the 5 Series’ rare dual character: calm luxury plus BMW driving pleasure
insights.description: Customers in both scoped markets value a car that is quiet and comfortable in normal use but still feels quick, precise and driver-focused. The successor should not trade away ride quality, cabin quietness or the feeling that “BMW puts the driver first”; sharper variants or settings may be needed for drivers who find the current car too soft or less stable than prior 5 Series models.

insights.title: Digital-first cabin needs fewer layers and more eyes-on-road controls
insights.description: Customers like advanced technology only when common tasks are fast, visible and low-distraction. Pain points appear around menu depth, screen-only controls, assistant/AC operation, cruise-gap changes and small navigation information; the successor needs clearer hierarchy plus tactile or shortcut access for frequent driving and comfort functions.

insights.title: Home charging should be programmable in customer language, not hidden behind departure-time logic
insights.description: Customers with time-of-use electricity plans want simple rules such as “start charging at 8:30 PM,” “charge any time on weekends,” and clear app feedback showing actual charging power. Inconsistent scheduled charging damages trust because owners cannot tell whether the car will obey their low-cost charging plan.

insight_caveats: US verbatims dominate the sample; EU conclusions often rely more on customer-study attributes and a small number of EU comments. Do not generalize US-only verbatim themes to EU without validation.
The package states that 279 verbatims from outside the selected markets were excluded from market-specific counts; insights above only use US/EU evidence provided here.

Sales context for prioritization: SALES:EU shows 115000 units in 2025 and 127000 in 2030; SALES:US shows 78000 units in 2025 and 80000 in 2030. These figures indicate both scoped markets remain relevant, but they are not customer-need evidence.
VFC topic statistics guide topic selection, but individual claims are supported with the cited feedback IDs and customer-study attributes listed in each insight.
